title: Failure probability for one-step CNF representation of DNF gates
statement:
Fix an integer $w \ge 1$ and let $D_1, \dots, D_{s_2}$ be DNF formulas over $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables, each of width at most $w$, and suppose that within every term of every $D_i$ no variable occurs more than once (distinct literals of a term have distinct underlying variables, and no literal is repeated). Let $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ (so in particular $p \le 1$), and draw a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, in which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Then for any target width $l$, the probability that some restricted gate $x \mapsto D_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ fails to be computed by any CNF formula of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  s_2\!\left( \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right) \right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: s₂ DNF gates on n variables (gates : Fin s₂ → DNF n)
each gate has width at most w
within each term, literals sharing a variable are identical (no variable in both polarities)
each term has no duplicate literals (Nodup)
conclusion: failure probability of admitting a width-≤l CNF for every gate is at most s₂((1/2)^l + exp(-np/3))
replaced:
For $s_2$ layer-2 DNF gates of width at most $w$ (with the usual no-duplicate-variable
and nodup hypotheses on terms) and a Bernoulli restriction with parameter
$p \le 1/(40w)$, the probability that some gate fails to admit a width-$\ell$ CNF
representation of its restriction is at most
$s_2 \cdot \left( (1/2)^{\ell} + \exp(-np/3) \right)$.
